title: Non-linearizable Root Group Data
summary: An RGD system $\mathcal{D}$ is called \emph{linear w.r.t. a root basis $\mathcal{B}$} if the commutation relations between the root groups of $\mathcal{D}$ are `linear' in a certain sense. Moreover, $\mathcal{D}$ is called \emph{linearizable}, if there exists a root basis $\mathcal{B}$ such that $\mathcal{D}$ is linear w.r.t. $\mathcal{B}$. For many examples of RGD systems it is easy to see that they are linear w.r.t. a concrete root basis.
